posts.description:
Been a while, here’s an update on what I’ve been up to this quarter:

- Visited Brown University as 1 of 3 students selected to explore its CS graduate program through the highly prestigious Brown Doctoral Preview Day.
- Started as a Data Analyst Intern at IDXExchange, analyzing housing market data and building Tableau dashboards.
- Joined Bruin Software Engineers’s loop engineering fellowship track, learning about AI agents and building a multi-agent system that ports DOOM to the browser.
- Leading a DataRes at UCLA Consulting project with Nokkomo Mints to better understand their customer demographics and identifying gaps in the market that they can target.
- Leading a CAIR Collective at UCLA project exploring how transformers and AI agents can improve clinical trial matching.
- Joined the Alignment Hive contributor track through the Mercial AI Safety Research Fellowship, building and testing an LLM classifier that decides which Claude Code sessions to share with AI safety researchers.

It's been a busy quarter, but I've really enjoyed learning new things, exploring new opportunities, and meeting new people along the way.  😇

posts.transcript: There's a great selection of who's startups that will change the AI landscape off tomorrow. Today we are at the Willard Bay Stadium for the AI pitch competition, in which startups are testing their own pitches. Not only support for them to meet coaches, but also each other as other startup founders, to learn from each other, to be resilient, to keep on going. And it helps, of course, them to be part of an ecosystem. The students, they had the the, the final chance to work on the pitch. We had a a table switching with mentors, which really helped giving outside the perspectives on our pitch. So it was really valuable. Almost everybody struggles with making choices. They want to solve it all in their pitch. They need to focus. The best advice I got today. Your key message super sharp and to the point. Make it personal. What is your personal drive? What is your why? Why did you start this company? So my main take away of today is to make my pitch and my storyline better accessible, understandable for broader audiences. I think if I hadn't joined today, my pitch wouldn't be as sharp as it will be on November 12th. So come check it out and see how well we will do.

posts.description:
Last week one of the biggest chapters of my life came to an end. I graduated from SIMC - Master in Strategy, Innovation and Management Control at WU (Wirtschaftsuniversität Wien) 🎓

Two years ago I moved to Vienna without knowing a single person. I had a new city, a new program I had only seen on paper, and no idea what would come of it.

Looking back, it became much more than a degree.
The program and its community changed how I think about strategy, startups and organisations, and also about what I want to build myself. I got to work on amazing projects, from early-stage startups to the World Food Programme. And to top it off, I spent a semester at the The University of British Columbia in Vancouver taking innovation and sustainability courses in the MBA program and exploring the Pacific Northwest on the side.

But if I’m honest, the best part was never in the curriculum.
Two years ago I didn’t know a single person here. Today I’m leaving with friends I know I’ll have for life. The late nights before deadlines, the countless SIMC events, the trips, and the people who turned a new city into home.
Thank you to my family for their continuous support, and to my classmates, professors and everyone who was part of these two years. 🫶
